IB CS · HL · Unit 8

Unit 8: Supervised & Unsupervised

HL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

How do computers learn without being explicitly programmed?

This unit dives into the algorithms of AI. You will distinguishing between Supervised Learning (Training with Teacher) and Unsupervised Learning (Self-Discovery). You will build Decision Trees, map Clusters, and understand why 'Overfitting' is the enemy of intelligence.

You'll start by teaching computers to classify data using K-Nearest Neighbours and Decision Trees. Then you'll remove the labels and let the machine find its own patterns using K-Means Clustering and Association Rules.

Supervised Learning (Labels)

The machine learns from examples (Inputs + Correct Answers).

  • K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN): "Tell me who your friends are, and I'll tell you who you are." Classifies based on proximity.
  • Decision Trees: A flowchart of questions (Is it red? Is it round?) to reach a conclusion.
Unsupervised Learning (Patterns)

The machine finds structure in chaos (No labels).

  • Clustering (K-Means): Grouping similar items together (e.g., Customer Segments).
  • Association Rules: "People who buy Bread also buy Butter" (Market Basket Analysis).
Tuning & Overfitting

Finding the Goldilocks Zone.

  • Hyperparameters: Settings we choose (like 'k' in KNN) before training.
  • Overfitting: Memorizing the training data perfectly but failing on new data (Bias/Variance trade-off).
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Supervised Learning Training a model on a labeled dataset (Input-Output pairs).
Unsupervised Learning Training a model to find patterns in unlabeled data.
K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) A classification algorithm that assigns a label based on the majority class of the 'k' closest data points.
Decision Tree A tree-like model of decisions and their possible consequences.
Clustering Grouping a set of objects in such a way that objects in the same group are more similar to each other.
Overfitting When a model learns the noise in the training data rather than the underlying pattern, performing poorly on new data.
Hyperparameter A configuration variable that is external to the model and whose value cannot be estimated from data (e.g., 'k').
Entropy A measure of impurity or disorder used in Decision Trees to decide where to split.
